items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And Grady Tate used to go BANG and hit a big hard rim shot. And then he’d say “leave the drums there.”

ctx.x: The opinions you get about him seem to be very different. Some people felt that he went out of his way to be nasty to them, and other people felt that he just was — that the music was —

That was his way of telling you he wanted something. He wanted the beat. He wanted to get the kick in the pants from you. And if you didn’t get it, he would harass you a little bit. I know I worked with Sonny Igoe who played with Benny a long time, maybe one of his last great bands, you know. It might have been the bebop band he had. That Benny looked at him, you know, gave him the bit, and looked at him straight in the eye, and Sonny went like this. And Benny never bothered him anymore. And Benny always used to…
Enough said. That’s good. Oh boy. What’s in the future for you, coming up?
